learningObjectives: Create classes and objects to model real-world entities.
Use constructors and instance variables to initialize objects.
Apply encapsulation to control access to object data.

activities.title: Class and Object Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the parts of a Java class and the object created from it.

content.concept: A class defines the fields and methods that describe a type of object. An object is an instance of that class with its own instance state.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Object Creation Flow
activities.instruction: Arrange the steps involved in creating an object.

content.concept: The new keyword creates an object and invokes an appropriate constructor. The resulting object reference can be stored in a variable and used to access its members.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

goal: 3. Use new to request an object

activities.title: Constructor Builder
activities.instruction: Build a constructor that initializes the object's fields.

content.concept: A constructor has the same name as its class and has no return type. Constructors can receive parameters and initialize instance variables when objects are created.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Encapsulation Strategy
activities.instruction: Choose the access strategy that protects object state.

content.concept: Encapsulation keeps internal state controlled by restricting direct access and exposing appropriate public methods. A common pattern is private fields with public getters and carefully designed setters.
